title: BehaviorEvent
description: Wire format for kernel-derived behavior records emitted by an in-VM tracer (reference producer: bloodhound). One UTF-8 NDJSON record per line. This schema is the workspace-canonical source of truth; producers and consumers vendor it with a commit pin (see docs/spec/behavior_event/README.md §4 for the compatibility model).

header.description: Correlation metadata shared across all event types.

timestamp.description: Wall-clock seconds since epoch (float for sub-second precision).

auid.description: Audit User ID (Login UID). Survives privilege escalation.

sessionid.description: Audit Session ID assigned by the kernel at login.

pid.description: Process ID that produced the event.

event.description: Classification of the captured behavior. The pedagogical layer (L1/L2/L3) is not encoded here; consumers derive it from (type, name) per docs/spec/behavior_event/README.md §3.

type.description: Source class of the event. SYSCALL/TTY/PACKET/KPROBE/TRACEPOINT/LSM are kernel-derived. LIFECYCLE is a userspace-synthesised process-lifecycle marker (process_start, process_fork, process_exit, thread_create). HEARTBEAT carries periodic drop / utilisation deltas. META carries tracer-internal lifecycle markers (e.g., bloodhound_ready, session_start).

name.description: Specific hook name (e.g., openat, tty_write) or META/LIFECYCLE/HEARTBEAT event name.

proc.description: Process context. Optional; fields are best-effort.

main_executable.description: Absolute path to the binary; best-effort, may be empty for short-lived processes.

cwd.description: Current working directory at event time.

args.description: Event-type-specific payload. Field set is producer-defined; consumers should treat unknown keys permissively. Common fields used by reference scenarios include filename, argv, flags, fd_type, data, syscall_nr, raw_args.

return_code.description: Exit code or syscall return value, when applicable.
